document.abstract: SMPTE ST 2110 supports both uncompressed ¹ and compressed video clippings, ² which allow it to be used in live production workflows for both high- and low-value content. However, high- and low-end live production require different quality and have very different budgets. In addition, although the entire quality spectrum will use the same set of standards, building a wide-area network (WAN) that provides the quality demanded by high-end live production, while also meeting the price pressure from low-end live production, is also challenging. The solution is a WAN that can seamlessly mix both private (dedicated) and public (Internet) infrastructures.

authors.bio: Alexander Sandstrom is a product manager with more than a decade of experience in streaming media and networking. At the time of writing this article, he was a strategic product manager at Net Insight, Stockholm, Sweden, providing broadcasters and media service providers IP and internet-based video contribution solutions. Prior to this, he was driving the shift to IP and software-defined networking (SDN) in telecoms by designing, selling, and marketing IP and SDN-based solutions at one of the world’s largest telecom vendors. He joined Amazon, Stockholm, Sweden, as a product manager for low-latency live streaming in the beginning of 2020.
